contents.text: A food chain is a model. A model can be used to show events in nature. Models can help make these events easier to understand. A food chain is a model that shows where living things in an ecosystem get their food.
A food chain has arrows that point from one living thing to another. Each arrow shows the direction that matter moves when one living thing eats another living thing.

Matter enters a food chain when a producer makes its own food. This is how all of the matter eaten by living things enters the food chain. Many producers make their own food using carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight. Producers do not eat other living things. So, there is no arrow pointing from another living thing to the producer in a food chain. Each food chain has one producer.
Matter first moves up a food chain when the producer is eaten by a consumer. This is shown by an arrow pointing from the producer to a consumer.
A consumer that hunts and eats another consumer is a predator. The consumer eaten by a predator is its prey. Matter moves up a food chain when a predator hunts and eats its prey.
